faqs.q: How do you tell storm damage from normal roof wear on a West Orange home?

runs.v: Storm damage shows a pattern: hail leaves random-pattern circular bruises with granule loss, and wind damage concentrates at the roof edges, rakes, and corners where uplift peaks, per IBHS wind and hail research. Uniform deterioration across the roof reads as wear, not a storm. On the exposed West Orange ridge, wind uplift and branch impact off South Mountain and Eagle Rock are the common storm patterns, per Essex County Parks terrain.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for storm damage roof repair in West Orange?

runs.v: Minor roof repairs typically need no municipal permit in New Jersey: a repair or replacement of the roof covering on a detached one- or two-family West Orange home counts as ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, per the NJ Uniform Construction Code. On a Main Street, Valley Road, or Route 280 commercial, multi-family, or attached building, a new roof or a repair of more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months requires a permit, and a construction permit may be required for structural repairs after storm damage; call the West Orange building department with permit questions before work begins.

faqs.q: Does storm repair on a West Orange historic landmark need extra approval?

runs.v: It can. A designated landmark or a property in a historic district can need extra review before exterior roofing work, so confirm requirements with the West Orange construction office first. faqs.q: Can storm damage be repaired, or does the roof need full replacement?

runs.v: Localized storm damage of a few shingles or a single puncture takes a targeted repair; under the contractor-consensus 25% rule, damage above 25 to 30% of the roof area takes full replacement, since replacement is necessary when damage is widespread. A second threshold, the 50% rule, favors replacement when one repair approaches 50% of replacement cost, per industry cost guidance. A roof that has served West Orange winters for two decades is often a replacement candidate, and proper installation is what lets a new roofing system reach a 20- to 40-year lifespan; GAF and Owens Corning shingles carry manufacturer warranties of up to 50 years.
